questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Philosophers espousing presentism (the view that only present things exist) must contend with the truth-maker objection (TO). TO: If past things don’t exist, what makes true statements about the past (e.g., “dinosaurs existed”) true? 1996: Presentist philosopher John Bigelow proposed “Lucretianism.” Lucretianism posits that the statement is made true by the world’s acceptance of the past-tensed property of “having contained dinosaurs.” 2006: Presentist philosopher Craig Bourne proposed “ersatz presentism.” Ersatz presentism posits that the statement is made true by an abstract (“ersatz”) time that exists outside temporal time and represents how things were in the past.
questions.prompt: The student wants to distinguish Bourne’s proposed theory from Bigelow’s. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: In contending with the truth-maker objection, ersatz presentism diverges from Lucretianism’s use of past-tensed properties by positing an “ersatz” time-outside-time capable of representing past things.
choices.B: Following Bigelow’s 1996 proposal, Bourne accepted the existence of past-tensed properties to solve the truth-maker problem with one caveat: a form of “ersatz” time that exists outside temporal time.
choices.C: The presentist approaches of Bigelow (1996) and Bourne (2006) differ in whether they consider truths about the past—the statement “dinosaurs existed,” for example—to be made true by anything at all.
choices.D: In 2006, Bourne proposed ersatz presentism, disagreeing with Bigelow’s earlier hypothesis that only present things exist.

questions.passage:

Prehistoric rock art in the Kimberley region of Australia consists of several distinct styles across various time periods. Irregular Infill Animal Period (IIAP) rock art from 13,000 to 17,000 years ago consists of naturalistic animal figures showing detailed features and a variety of poses. Gwion rock art from 12,000 to 14,000 years ago features elaborately ornamented anthropomorphic figures. Wanjina rock art from up to 5,000 years ago features human ancestor figures along with animal motifs. A 2025 study of Kimberley rock art by Ana Paula Motta et al. identified 98 figures depicting outlines of animal forms with simple anatomical details and posed predominantly in profile. The study’s superimposition analysis showed that these Linear Naturalistic Figures (LNF) consistently appear on top of Gwion and underneath Wanjina figures.
questions.prompt: The student wants to make and support a claim about the LNF rock art style based on Motta et al.’s study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The distinct style displayed by the LNF rock art forms a bridge between the styles of the earlier IIAP animal figures and the later Gwion representations of humans.
choices.B: The LNF rock art should be considered its own distinct style because its depictions of animal forms reveal a categorical departure from the art of the previous period.
choices.C: The differences between the LNF rock art and earlier IIAP depictions of animals show a notable increase in detail and variety, proving that rock art figures became more detailed over time.
choices.D: The study by Motta et al. showed that the LNF figures were clearly layered in between anthropomorphic figures of distinct styles that took place millennia apart.
